blocks.text: Aslam Khan’s call is answered by volunteers who say they were prepared to reach Lahore voluntarily and need no special escort or inducement so long as the campaign against the Singhs moves forward.

Their zeal takes visible form when they planted a Haidri flag and announced that those without any means could join their ranks, turning the movement into a broad religious mobilization rather than a narrow state order.
The page also begins naming patrons and early participants, including Murtaza Khan, to show how elite backing and street-level fervour merged into one anti-Khalsa front.
